claim: Merchant onboarding took 21 days and was losing deals to faster competitors, so I redesigned the workflow around automated identity checks and a single case owner, cutting onboarding to 6 days.
Manual reconciliation consumed 14 analysts and delayed settlement, so I automated matching and exception routing, removing GBP 3.2m of annual run cost without service loss.

A chargeback backlog of 4,800 cases was putting merchant relationships at risk, so I introduced a daily triage cell with clear ownership and ageing targets, clearing the backlog to 300 cases in 12 weeks.
Operations was a set of disconnected teams with no shared routines, so I restructured it into three accountable teams with a weekly management rhythm, now 62 people across London and Manchester.
The prior year FCA safeguarding review raised 7 major findings, so I rebuilt the controls, evidence packs and reconciliation sign-off, and the next audit closed with zero major findings.
Support agents spent too long reading case histories, so I piloted AI-assisted case summaries and triage with human review, reducing average handling time by 35 percent.
Stock write-offs were eroding margin, so I introduced cycle counts and a weekly variance review with store managers, recovering GBP 1.4m of write-offs in the first year.
Every store ran its own routines, so I wrote and rolled out a single operations playbook with store manager input, adopted across 140 stores in 9 months.
Back-office teams worked to inconsistent standards with high rework, so I ran a Lean programme across 5 teams, delivering GBP 4.1m of verified savings over two years.
Loan servicing errors ran at 6.2 percent and drove complaints, so I introduced checklists, root cause reviews and first-time-right targets, bringing errors down to 1.8 percent.
Operations was spread over three sites with duplicated roles, so I designed a new operating model for 220 people consolidated onto two sites with no compulsory redundancies.
Complaints took 38 days to resolve on average, so I created a single complaints queue with named owners and weekly ageing reviews, reducing resolution time to 12 days.
New team leaders were promoted without management training, so I ran a coaching programme for 18 team leaders to build the habits that held the Lean gains in place.

The retailer had no click-and-collect offer while competitors did, so I led the cross-functional programme that launched it in 300 stores in 10 months, generating GBP 18m of online revenue in the first year.
Programme spending was poorly controlled, so I introduced stage gates and monthly financial reviews across a GBP 25m portfolio, with 94 percent of projects landing on budget.
Programme reporting took 5 days each month and arrived too late to act on, so I built a programme office with standard templates and a live dashboard covering 30 projects, cutting reporting to 1 day.
Failed deliveries ran at 9 percent and drove repeat costs, so I introduced delivery windows and driver route reviews, bringing failures down to 4 percent and saving GBP 900k.
Warehouse pick rates varied widely between depots, so I introduced slotting changes and daily performance boards, lifting pick rates by 22 percent across 3 depots.
Overtime was covering poor shift planning for 85 staff, so I rebuilt rotas around forecast demand, cutting overtime cost by GBP 350k a year.
Month-end reporting took 6 days and delayed trading decisions, so I automated the data pulls and built the first KPI dashboard, cutting the cycle to 2 days.
